the microvascular no-reflow is a major determinant of infarct size, and is a predictor of adverse clinical outcomes in patients with acute MI.
the no-reflow phenomenon is an important determinant of myocardial salvage after acute myocardial infraction (AMI).

In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the microvascular no-reflow (MR) phenomenon using Tc-99m MAA scintigraphy in acute myocardial infraction (AMI) patients.
the development of an automated method for the analysis of microcirculation in patients with acute MI.
the assessment of "microvascular non-reflow phenomenon" in patients with acute anterior wall myocardial infarcts.

the use of Tc-99m macro-aggregated albumin (MAA) scintigraphy for the assessment of microvascular no-reflow is not yet recommended.
the evidence supports the use of the 2014 ACC/AHA guidelines for the management of patients with STEMI.
the use of the term "microvascular no-re-flow phenomenon" in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarctions undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention is a misnomer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study of the microvasculature in patients with acute coronary syndromes is important, and that the use of Tc-99m macro-aggregated albumin (MAA) scanning is an effective method of assessing this.
we have demonstrated that the "no-reflow phenomenon" is a frequent finding in acute myocardial infariation and that it is not related to coronary artery spasm or to coronary artery embolization.
the results of this study show the potential for a noninvasive method to detect the microvascular no-reflow phenomena.

the microvascular no-reflow (MNR) phenomenon is a common finding in patients with STEMI.
the no-reflow phenomenon is an independent predictor of mortality in patients with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarctions.
